scope: Eight active Plecopedia source-link proposals; classify original description versus comparison, geography, or breeder context

records.interpretation: 2016 original description explicitly references Panaqolus sp. L398, but does not prove a sold aquarium specimen matches its type series.
claimsNotProven: any similar Xingu population is the same species

records.interpretation: Original authors named tankei in honor of Andreas Tanke and wrote 'probably' first to reproduce the species; this is a qualified attribution, not independent verification of all breeding claims.
The 2016 paper describes P. tankei/L398, not L397; L397 is a distinct trade form. A 2015 Catfish Study Group article records a particular keeper's L397 spawning observations.
claimsNotProven: general breeding success across all lineages

records.interpretation: The 2009 original description directly uses L239 and blue panaque as trade names for described B. beggini; genus assignment was originally tentative, and individual stock still requires ID.
claimsNotProven: any traded blue pleco is taxonomically authenticated

records.interpretation: 2010 original work describes P. titan from Ecuador Napo; IUCN 2023 discusses L191 from Colombian Caqueta as commercially identified P. titan but treats Colombian occurrence uncertain/cf. titan.
claimsNotProven: L191 and L418 identical by genetics

records.interpretation: Original P. titan description is Napo Ecuador; IUCN 2023 associates L418 with Huallaga Peru trade fish. Do not treat that commercial source region as verified type locality.
claimsNotProven: Peruvian L418 authenticated to Ecuador type
L191 identical to L418 by lineage

records.taxonDescribed: Two new Baryancistrus species from Trombetas, not Baryancistrus niveatus
records.interpretation: The 2025 Trombetas study reviews B. niveatus as an existing comparison; B. niveatus was originally described by Castelnau 1855, not in this study.
2010 Zootaxa paper describes P. compta/L134; does not make L015 P. compta or establish L015 as P. vittata.
